pages.title: What it does
text: It sets how much extra damage a crit deals: final critical multiplier = 1.5 + critical damage / 100.
With 0 critical damage the multiplier is 1.5 (vanilla); 50 points -> 2.0x; 100 -> 2.5x; 200 -> 3.5x.
It only matters when the critical chance roll says the hit is a crit, so the two stats belong together.

pages.title: Flat (numeric) line
text: The curve is LINEAR: +1.0 percentage point per point, no ceiling.

pages.title: Percent line
text: Also LINEAR: +2% per point, on the DESIGN_BASELINE basis with reference B_ref = 50 percentage points.
Contribution = 50 * (2 * points) / 100 = +1.0 percentage point per point.

In other words, with the shipped defaults the flat and percent lines are worth exactly the same per point (+1 percentage point each). The percent line matters when you raise basis_value, or when you want to constrain it with its own curve or max_points.
The two contributions add up to your final critical damage value.

pages.title: Ceiling & returns
text: There is no ceiling: this stat is not a probability and does not change any mechanic, it only scales a damage number, so it can grow forever.
Its limit follows the attribute's own range (1.0E9), which is unreachable in practice - a numeric backstop only.
With diminishing returns gone it is a purely linear dimension: +1.0 percentage point per point, and with the shipped defaults both lines are identical.

pages.title: Practical advice
text: Critical damage is only worth as much as your critical chance: at 10% chance, +100 percentage points is effectively +10% damage overall.
Recommended route: take critical chance to 25%..35%, then pour points into critical damage.
With the default configuration the two lines are equivalent, so pick either or split evenly; if you plan to raise B_ref, favour the percent line.
